lines.text: You hit send. And one second later, you spot the typo, in a very dangerous place.
You meant the staging database. One word apart, and a world of difference.
Agents are fast and literal. It does not ask whether you meant it. It simply starts.
The fix is a small buffer between your finger and the agent. That is a send delay.
You turn it on in settings, and pick how many seconds Agent R Q should wait.
Now Agent R Q holds your message for a few seconds before it reaches the agent.
Inside that window you spot the typo, and you still have time to act on it.
Send Now skips the wait when you are sure. Cancel pulls the message back.
You cancel. The message never reaches the agent, and the database is exactly as you left it.
You fix the typo, send again, and let the countdown finish this time.
The agent acts on the right target, and the only database that disappears is staging.
Ever sent a message to an agent and instantly regretted it? Confess in the comments, and find send delay at Agent R Q dot com.
